en.html:
Suddenly I felt somebody looking at me. I raised my head.

Across the room, around the room—nobody.

Everything exactly as before I began the paper.

...Mera vaham? Had I imagined it?

Back to the page. Where had I reached? I tried to find my place, and there it was: a scribbled sentence in one corner.

The handwriting was untidy, unlike the main text. Still, it seemed to belong to the same hand.

Different language also. The paper mixed English and Yamato. This scrawl was German.

One sentence, apparently written in a single rush.

Mein... Machthabar...
Kristallnacht...

When I had been desperately hunting a treatment for my sister, I had picked up a little German. Medicine was advanced in Germany; therefore German had also become my problem.

Now I turned that unreliable memory upside down. Scraped the bottom. Kuch toh must be left. Somehow I assembled a translation that made sense.

Probably, the sentence said:

'My Great Law-Head, what happened on the Night of Crystal?'

en.html:
A girl.

Since when?

A few dozen seconds ago I had looked around this very room. Surely she had not been there. Or... had she? Looking straight at her and still overlooking her—that also seemed possible.

Ridiculous, but I had to consider it. There was so little insistence about her. I am here. I am a person. Even that much announcement she did not make.

Hardly any human presence reached me. Blood should be circulating, a heart should be beating, and yet this much of an object she seemed.

en.html:
A ridiculous idea. Still, dismissing it outright was not possible. The girl was quiet and motionless beyond any reasonable limit.

Slowly I reached out a finger and touched her cheek.

Soft.
Warm.

Skin, with body heat. Haan, a living person after all, apparently.

Words had done nothing. Touch, perhaps, counted as a stimulus: she blinked. Then she looked steadily up at me.

And went on looking.
Not the smallest movement.

en.text:
A tall man was there.

A full beard, and eyes roaming here, there, everywhere. Attention, this man knew how to demand.

Beside the statue-like girl, he was human with considerable enthusiasm. Age, not so clear. Getting on, at first glance. Then some things suggested he might be surprisingly young. Surely not in his thirties, though.

As for me—◆he simply looked straight past me. Then he saw the girl beside him, and his whole face broke into a smile.

Wolf"One doubt has been living very comfortably in my mind for years."
Kageaki"What doubt?"
Wolf"Why does humanity insist on speaking correctly? Kya mil raha hai? What great reward?"
Kageaki"...You mean in the philosophical sense?"
Wolf"That description will do. But zara socho—nobody enters the world with command of the subjunctive. Afterward we are learning it, practicing it, making such efforts to get everything correct."
Wolf"Everybody doing it, as though destiny itself had enrolled us in grammar tuition."
Wolf"Then we become excited, and what comes out? Noise! Glorious noise, answerable to no grammar. First get correct, then get happy, and correctness has already left. What is the sense in this arrangement?"
Kageaki"Some people do without correct speech from the beginning."
Wolf"Yes, and what do we call them? Violators! Incorrect against a correct society. Our rule remains; they have not escaped it."
Kageaki"For particular tastes, then."
Wolf"But the ordinary people abandon it eventually too. If everyone is going there, why make such elaborate preparations to start somewhere else?"
Wolf"TOH DON'T START! No correctness, no need to demolish correctness! Whole arrangement unnecessary!"

Kageaki"...I see. I understand the point."
Wolf"Good. Then you are with me."
Kageaki"No."
Wolf"NO!?"
Kageaki"People should speak correctly."
Wolf"Why?"
Kageaki"This time, let me ask you something."
Wolf"Go on."
Kageaki"Suppose someone spoke nothing but incomprehensible nonsense to you. Would that make you happy?"
Wolf"Are you trying to insult me?"
Kageaki"Please answer."
Wolf"I would inform him, at considerable volume, that making sounds is not the same as making sense. Then demand ONE sentence fit for human use!"
Kageaki"So you would have to correct him. Would you enjoy that work?"
Wolf"Enjoy? Already I am tired, and the fellow is not even here!"
Kageaki"The reverse, then. Take a fine, proper sentence and make a wreck of it. By choice."
Wolf"Wah! That is life giving you its best part."
Kageaki"There you have it."
Wolf"Have what?"
Kageaki"If everyone talks nonsense, you must keep repairing other people's sentences. If people ordinarily speak properly, you can choose a particularly fine sentence and ruin it at your leisure. Which life would you choose?"
Kageaki"Answer is clear, no?"
Wolf"————————"
Wolf"OHH!!"

Already I am tired, and the fellow is not even here!"Kageaki"The reverse, then. Take a fine, proper sentence and make a wreck of it. By choice."Wolf"Wah! That is life giving you its best part."Kageaki"There you have it."Wolf"Have what?"Kageaki"If everyone talks nonsense, you must keep repairing other people's sentences. If people ordinarily speak properly, you can choose a particularly fine sentence and ruin it at your leisure. Which life would you choose?"Kageaki"Answer is clear, no?"Wolf"————————"Wolf"OHH!!"

ほど暇ではないだろう。当たり前である。

en.html:
Kageaki"...As a prisoner, I consider the treatment reasonably proper. Active hostility, therefore, I am not intending."
Kageaki"So long as your request does not seriously harm my interests or those of people connected with me, Professor, whatever is possible from my side I shall do."
Wolf"Haan, haan. No need for such a grand arrangement."
Wolf"A small matter. Immediately settled."
Kageaki"...Sir."
Wolf"Are you healthy?"
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"Yes. Bodily functions are mostly working without difficulty."
Wolf"By tomorrow morning you will not have accidentally become dead, na?"
Kageaki"...Mostly, I think that is unlikely."
Wolf"Good. Work finished. Back to your room you may go."
Wolf"The soldier who brought you here is waiting outside."
